notes: The September edition — the free rehearsal for the two sibling ledgers, and the one that finds their instrument is pointed at the wrong sheet. THE CENTRAL FINDING: `existing-home-sales-2026-11-12`'s first kill switch reads "No `ContribArchives` vintage dated 2026-10-13 exists by 2026-10-16." That cannot be observed, by construction rather than by chance. `ContribArchives` in GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx (re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 from /-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/…; the path the earliest sibling ledgers cite 404s) is a strict concatenation of 49 COMPLETED-QUARTER blocks — 0 of 49 overlap, every block runs from the quarter's initial nowcast to its final one — and it currently ends 2026-07-28, the last 2026:Q2 vintage. The live 2026:Q3 run is not missing, it is elsewhere in the same workbook: `ContribHistory` and `CurrentQtrEvolution` carry 17 vintages, 2026-07-30 → 2026-09-03. A 2026-10-13 vintage is a 2026:Q3 vintage, and the Fed's own PostedUpdates puts the "Final nowcast of 2026:Q3" on 2026-10-28 — so the Q3 block cannot reach `ContribArchives` before then, and the switch would fire as a FALSE POSITIVE on 2026-10-16 whatever GDPNow actually posts. The amendment handed back to both siblings is the SHEET, not the date: the same observation is available on the day itself in `ContribHistory`/`CurrentQtrEvolution`. The defect also reaches FT-existing-home-sales-2026-11-12-1 and -2 (a 2026:Q4 vintage scored by 2026-11-18) and puts existing-home-sales-2026-09-10's -3/-4 (Q3 vintages scored 2026-11-15) on a schedule that only holds if the Q3 block publishes within 18 days of closing. SECOND FINDING, also a correction: both siblings carry a kill switch at "the vintage moves residential investment by ≥0.30pp," described as far past anything in the class. Measured, it is 5 of 123 solo EHS vintages (4.1%) — and all five immediately followed a HOUSING-STARTS vintage, while 0 of the 22 that followed anything else ever cleared it (max 0.2021pp). NAR's 2026 calendar moved EHS ahead of housing starts: 111 of 133 EHS vintages 2014-2025 followed starts, 0 of 7 in 2026 do, and 2026's seven Δresidential readings top out at 0.0595pp. The switch was a housing-starts detector riding on the EHS vintage, and the 2026 reordering disconnected it. THIRD: 10-13 is unscheduled on PostedUpdates, the shape that has produced a SOLO existing-home-sales vintage on 6 of 6 unscheduled 2026 dates — now including 2026-08-11, out of sample for both siblings. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` re-derived on 2,514 daily sessions 2016-09-06 → 2026-09-04 (Nasdaq API), reproducing both siblings within 0.01pp: 114 EHS release days leave SPY (p=0.66), ITB (p=0.58) and XHB (p=0.45) at baseline and the 100 solo ones do too; a re-run grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md returns 0 housing hits, so no instrument attaches. The session's own shape is new — 0 of 114 past EHS releases landed the session after a bond-market-only closure — but both components measure flat: after a bond-only closure ITB 1.779% vs 1.872% (n=20, p=0.67), one session before a CPI vintage ITB 1.880% vs 1.872% (n=113, p=0.92). Unlike its 09-10 sibling it sits OUTSIDE any FOMC blackout (the 10-28 meeting's window opens 2026-10-17), which removes the one regime measured to widen homebuilders. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the call is stand aside on every horizon. Proposed twice in-sweep on 2026-09-08 (from-existing-home-sales-2026-09-10, from-pending-home-sales-2026-09-17); this canonical file, written by the event's own initial research, shadows both.
